StartupBoundaryTests.Frontend_subscripti.reason: The source textual AfterPlatformServicesSetup/host.Start/classic-lifetime ordering and forbidden repository/worker registrations are replaced by actual Electron native-readiness observations and the recursive frontend dependency boundary. The native wrapper records app.isReady for every real loopback fetch, including SSE subscription, and every BrowserWindow; the real companion owns repositories and workers in a separate process. The renderer animation worker remains permitted; it is not a backend ingest/enrichment/session worker. Desktop and fullscreen run the same external-backend boundary.

StartupBoundaryTests.Every_async_void_li.reason: The original recursively scans C# App files for protected override async void methods, requires a nonempty result, parses each method body by brace depth and requires catch. This disposition does not waive asynchronous error handling: the real primary renderer-load Promise is observed through the startup failure boundary, failed native loading reports exit 3 once, and closed-window/quit cancellation consumes late rejection without an alert. The separate backend retains its independent lifetime.

StartupBoundaryTests.The_startup_spine_i.reason: All three original source rows remain represented: Program startup reporting becomes the guarded app.whenReady/initialize chain; MainWindow startup-load reporting becomes awaited primary loadURL plus the controlled renderer preparation failure/retry boundary; theme.LoadAsync becomes validated appearance hydration and a guarded module-load fallback. Actual process failures retain useful redacted diagnostics and exit 3. The primary load rejects into that same boundary rather than becoming an unhandled Promise, and initial activations cannot construct a window while a fatal companion result is still pending. Startup health and preference waiting share the existing 45-second frontend deadline; missing/slow backend attachment remains recoverable and cancellation closes timers/listeners cleanly.

The backend remains external and all data lives in a disposable directory.

The explicit backend request replaces the source library-load invalidation/optional-DI branch without inventing a second scoring implementation or a nullable React library model.

StartupReadThreadTests.Library_and_start.reason: The fixture retains exact LibraryReadFixtures.Seed(20): 20 works/releases/Steam ownerships and the ordered Try next release list [20, 1], seeded before the first host response. The actual first API library request records one coherent snapshot lease and 20/20/20 work/ownership/bucket publication; the HTTP adapter additionally performs three explicit preference leases, all recorded rather than claimed to be the source total 1. Both real renderers visibly publish 20 games and the list in Game 20/Game 1 order, then load the actual Merge queue, Appearance and Library settings. Every recorded repository lease belongs to the backend process, distinct from both Electron main and renderer; HTTP thread-pool reads have no UI synchronization context, and actual DOM publication establishes the browser UI boundary. This process separation replaces Avalonia Dispatcher.CheckAccess/PropertyChanged-thread instrumentation without omitting the three later startup models.
